claims.text: Localized chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr restricts dislocation mobility relative to a chemically random state.
Chemical short-range order modifies the elevated-temperature lattice dynamics of HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical short-range order causes higher yield strength than a chemically random state.
Chemical short-range order reduces the thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical short-range order alters the elastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr relative to a random state.
Annealing protocols can produce pronounced chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Rapid quenching can produce a predominantly random HfNbTaTiZr atomic arrangement lacking significant short-range order.
Local atomic arrangements influence lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Local atomic arrangements influence dislocation interactions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range order enhances lattice distortion, which impedes dislocation migration.
Short-range order constrains atomic vibrations in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range order makes HfNbTaTiZr harder than its random-alloy state.
Short-range order makes HfNbTaTiZr stiffer than its random-alloy state.
Short-range order produces slower plastic relaxation, including limited dislocation re-emission after stress relief.
Localized stiffening caused by short-range order lowers the effective thermal expansion coefficient.
The short-range-ordered alloy will exhibit delayed plasticity onset or reduced relaxation in its elevated-temperature stress–strain response.
Short-range order increases the plastic-zone size and dislocation density in simulated HfNbTaTiZr nanoindentation.
The proposed short-range-order effects should be observable from 300°C to 900°C, particularly near the elastic-to-plastic transition.
Outside 300°C to 900°C or at extreme deformation rates, additional mechanisms may cause deviations from the proposed behavior.
Direct experimental quantification of short-range-order effects on thermal expansion and elastic response remains challenging.
